_README: Hand-written flavour, keyed by player name. bake-cards.mjs grafts these onto the auto-fetched facts, so re-baking never clobbers your voice. Add anyone you like — 'honors' is the DID YOU KNOW line, 'note' is the SCOUTING NOTE box.

Patrick Mahomes.honors: 3× Super Bowl champion. Fastest QB to 200 career passing TDs.
Patrick Mahomes.note: The face of the league — Kansas City's window stays open as long as he's upright.

Josh Allen.honors: 2024 NFL MVP. Buffalo's franchise leader in rushing touchdowns by a quarterback.
Josh Allen.note: Bulldozer with a cannon. The whole offense is a referendum on his arm.

Lamar Jackson.honors: Two-time NFL MVP, one of them unanimous. First QB with two 1,000-yard rushing seasons.
Lamar Jackson.note: The most dangerous open-field runner to ever play the position.

Joe Burrow.honors: Led Cincinnati to Super Bowl LVI. Best single-season completion percentage in NFL history.
Joe Burrow.note: Cool as anything in a two-minute drill. Health is the only real question.

Jalen Hurts.honors: Super Bowl LIX MVP. Holds the record for rushing touchdowns by a QB in a Super Bowl.
Jalen Hurts.note: Turned the quarterback sneak into an unstoppable offensive philosophy.

C.J. Stroud.honors: 2023 Offensive Rookie of the Year, with the best rookie passer rating of the modern era.
C.J. Stroud.note: Houston's franchise is fully rebuilt around his poise.

Jayden Daniels.honors: 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year and a Heisman winner. Reached the NFC Championship as a rookie.
Jayden Daniels.note: Instantly made the Commanders relevant again. Rare poise for his age.

Caleb Williams.honors: Heisman winner and No. 1 overall pick. Fewest interceptions by a rookie with 500+ attempts.
Caleb Williams.note: Improviser with a gunslinger streak. Chicago's offense is being built to his shape.

Brock Purdy.honors: The only 'Mr. Irrelevant' — last pick of the draft — ever to start a Super Bowl.
Brock Purdy.note: The most efficient value contract in football, right up until the extension landed.

Justin Herbert.honors: Offensive Rookie of the Year, and the fastest player ever to 20,000 career passing yards.
Justin Herbert.note: Prototype arm talent. A run-first system is the new variable.

Ja'Marr Chase.honors: 2024 receiving Triple Crown — led the NFL in catches, yards and touchdowns.
Ja'Marr Chase.note: Burrow's college roommate and the most bankable target in football.

Justin Jefferson.honors: Fastest to 5,000 career receiving yards. Highest yards-per-game average all-time.
Justin Jefferson.note: The Griddy is his, but the route running is what scares coordinators.

CeeDee Lamb.honors: Holds the Cowboys' single-season receptions record. Wears the franchise's legendary No. 88.
CeeDee Lamb.note: Carries the Dallas passing game whether or not it's convenient.

Tyreek Hill.honors: Nicknamed 'Cheetah.' Came within 61 yards of the single-season receiving record.
Tyreek Hill.note: Still the fastest man in the sport when the track is dry.

Amon-Ra St. Brown.honors: A fourth-round pick who set the Lions' single-season receptions record.
Amon-Ra St. Brown.note: The Sun God. Detroit's toughness in wide receiver form.

Puka Nacua.honors: Holds the NFL rookie records for both receptions and receiving yards.
Puka Nacua.note: A fifth-rounder who broke records nobody expected to fall.

Travis Kelce.honors: Most receiving yards by a tight end in playoff history. Seven straight 1,000-yard seasons.
Travis Kelce.note: The most decorated tight end of his era, on and off the field.

George Kittle.honors: Once held the single-season receiving yards record for a tight end.
George Kittle.note: Blocks like a tackle, runs like a receiver, celebrates like nobody's watching.

Brock Bowers.honors: Broke the NFL rookie record for receptions by a tight end.
Brock Bowers.note: Instantly the best thing about the Raiders offense.

Saquon Barkley.honors: Ninth player ever to rush for 2,000 yards in a season — then won the Super Bowl.
Saquon Barkley.note: The reverse hurdle is now a permanent part of NFL highlight reels.

Christian McCaffrey.honors: One of only three players with 1,000 rushing and 1,000 receiving yards in the same season.
Christian McCaffrey.note: When healthy, the most complete offensive weapon in football.

Derrick Henry.honors: Rushed for 2,027 yards in 2020. Heisman winner. 'King Henry.'
Derrick Henry.note: Still running defenders over well past the age backs are supposed to fall off.

Bijan Robinson.honors: Doak Walker Award winner and a top-10 pick at a position teams stopped drafting early.
Bijan Robinson.note: Atlanta's offense goes exactly as far as he carries it.

Jahmyr Gibbs.honors: Half of Detroit's 'Sonic and Knuckles' backfield.
Jahmyr Gibbs.note: Breakaway speed that turns a four-yard crease into six points.

Myles Garrett.honors: 2023 Defensive Player of the Year and the Browns' all-time sack leader.
Myles Garrett.note: A one-man pass rush on a roster that keeps asking him to be exactly that.

Micah Parsons.honors: Most sacks by any player in his first three NFL seasons since the stat became official.
Micah Parsons.note: Traded in a blockbuster — now terrorizing the NFC North from the other side.

T.J. Watt.honors: Tied the NFL single-season sack record with 22.5 in just 15 games.
T.J. Watt.note: Forces more fumbles than anyone alive. The Steelers defense begins and ends with him.

Nick Bosa.honors: Only the second player to win both Defensive Rookie of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year.
Nick Bosa.note: The engine of San Francisco's front four.

Aidan Hutchinson.honors: Was on a record sack pace in 2024 before a season-ending leg injury.
Aidan Hutchinson.note: Detroit's defensive identity — the comeback is the story to watch.

Sauce Gardner.honors: Never allowed a touchdown in his college career. First-team All-Pro as a rookie.
Sauce Gardner.note: Quarterbacks simply stopped looking at his side of the field.

Patrick Surtain II.honors: 2024 Defensive Player of the Year — the first cornerback to win it since 2009.
Patrick Surtain II.note: The rare corner good enough to win an award built for pass rushers.

Andy Reid.honors: One of only six coaches with 280+ career wins. Three Super Bowl titles in Kansas City.
Andy Reid.note: Still the best game-week play designer in football, cheeseburger jokes notwithstanding.

Kyle Shanahan.honors: His outside-zone scheme is the most copied offensive system of the last decade.
Kyle Shanahan.note: The league's most imitated play-caller, still hunting the ring.

Sean McVay.honors: Youngest head coach in modern NFL history — and the youngest ever to win a Super Bowl.
Sean McVay.note: Spawned an entire generation of thirty-something head coaching hires.

Dan Campbell.honors: Took Detroit from 3-13-1 to the NFC's No. 1 seed in three seasons.
Dan Campbell.note: The most aggressive fourth-down coach in the league, and the most quotable.

Mike Tomlin.honors: Has never had a losing season in his entire head coaching career.
Mike Tomlin.note: The longest active streak of respectability in professional sports.

John Harbaugh.honors: Won Super Bowl XLVII against his own brother's team.
John Harbaugh.note: Built the offense entirely around Lamar and never looked back.
